writeup.headline: Valero rates Buy on strong growth, momentum and low absolute multiples, but sits just above Hold.
writeup.thesis: Valero scores 67, a Buy, driven mainly by a strong trend score of 83: shares are up 127.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and are 46.9 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth scores 74 on TTM revenue growth of 24.6% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 43.3% year on year, though growth slowed by 5.5 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 69: in absolute terms the multiples are low, with P/S of 0.7x and EV/EBIT of 6.1x, while against its own history the overall picture is near the middle of its own history, with P/S more expensive than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends. Quality is the weak spot at 46, reflecting a thin 12.3% gross margin and 11.5% operating margin, partly offset by diluted share count down 7.8% year on year. News is mildly positive, with a Q3 earnings beat, a record refining margin of $39.24/bbl and mostly raised broker targets.
key_risks: Record refining margins came from supply disruptions and may not persist, which would hit growth and earnings.
Growth slowed by 5.5 pp from the previous quarter, and Q4 throughput guidance is modestly below Q3.
After a large run, the price is 15.5% below its 52-week high and 1.8% below its 50-day average, so momentum could fade.
P/S is more expensive than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends, leaving less room if margins normalize.
Industry policy moves, such as EPA's small-refinery-exemption proposal, could affect refiners.
what_would_change: A drop of 3 points would move the rating to Hold, for example if the trend score weakens or growth keeps decelerating.
Reaching Strong Buy would take 13 more points, likely needing better quality scores, such as higher margins, alongside sustained growth.
Fading refining margins or negative guidance and analyst news would pull growth and news risk scores down.
